texts: good. the proposing, Hesper, the experiment and its three water sources are all covered. Same caveat as elsewhere and on our side, not yours: "day 425 of Year 2" is stored with the day term we use for a day-of-month, and no rewrite avoids that.
good. the approving, the Council as approver and the same experiment from the previous sentence are all covered.

mixed: everything but the label parses well — Hesper as the filler, the cauldron, the sea-water it was filled with, and the Salt-bloom Tide-pools as that water's origin — but "the first" is dropped, because an enumerative ordinal has no slot in our ordinal head, so a later question naming "the first cauldron" cannot bind anything. Give the three cauldrons proper names instead, and use the same name at every later mention: "Hesper filled Cauldron One with sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools."

mixed: the filling, the sea-water and the deep ebb as its origin are all covered, but "the second" is dropped for the same reason as in the previous sentence, so nothing in the parse says which cauldron this is. Name it: "Hesper filled Cauldron Two with sea-water from the deep ebb."

mixed: the filling, the harbor water and the middle of the pier as its origin (with the middle correctly a part of the pier) are all covered, but "the third" is dropped like the other two labels. Name it: "Hesper filled Cauldron Three with harbor water from the middle of the pier."
good. the boiling, Hesper, the silken threads, all three cauldrons as the place (with the three individual cauldrons linked in as members of that set) and the one-day duration are all covered.

mixed: the forming of mire-essence and the cauldron it formed in are covered, but "the first" is dropped again, so this result cannot be tied to a named cauldron by a later question. Use the same name as in the filling sentence: "Mire-essence formed in Cauldron One."

mixed: the yield is covered and the one-vessel amount is kept, but "the first" is dropped as before — rewrite as "Cauldron One yielded one vessel of mire-essence." Separately, the amount is stored under an invented dimension word instead of our reserved "no dimension stated" marker; that is a defect on our side, not something your phrasing causes, so no further rewrite is needed for it.
mixed: the forming and the cauldron it formed in are covered, but "the second" is dropped. Rewrite as "Mire-essence formed in Cauldron Two."

mixed: as with the first cauldron's yield, the one-vessel amount is kept but "the second" is dropped, so rewrite as "Cauldron Two yielded one vessel of mire-essence." The invented dimension word on the amount is again ours to fix, not yours.

mixed: the denial is right — no forming of mire-essence, with the substance, the forming and the cauldron all kept inside the denied claim — but "the third" is dropped, so the cauldron that failed is unnamed. Rewrite as "No mire-essence formed in Cauldron Three."
mixed: the yield of chalky residue is covered, with "chalky" correctly kept as a separate description of the residue, but "the third" is dropped. Rewrite as "Cauldron Three yielded chalky residue."
good. Hesper as the reporter, the results as what was reported and the Council as the addressee are all covered.
good. the Council as the recorder, the same results as what was recorded, and the ledger as where they were written are all covered.
